findings.requirement: AC-17b: project_hard_deleted event survives cascade; ProjectHardDeleteJobTest verifies correct cascade order
findings.detail: The Architecture 'Hard-delete cron' section (lines 82-86) was correctly fixed to: (1) cascade-delete events first, (2) emit project_hard_deleted events, (3) delete project documents. However the Testing Strategy unit test description for ProjectHardDeleteJobTest (line 298) still reads 'cascade order = emit event → delete events → delete projects' — the OLD broken order that was the subject of round-1 finding 1. The unit test description now contradicts the Architecture. A developer implementing the job from the tech-spec will see conflicting instructions: Architecture says delete-events-first, test description says emit-first. If the developer follows the test description, the bug from round 1 is reintroduced. This must be corrected before implementation.

findings.requirement: AC-17 / AC-17b: Audit event table comment for project_hard_deleted
findings.detail: The Audit event types table (line 269) entry for project_hard_deleted still carries the parenthetical '(event itself survives cascade — written before remove)'. With the corrected Architecture ordering (cascade delete first, then emit, then delete projects), the comment 'written before remove' is now misleading — the event is written AFTER the cascade delete of prior events and BEFORE project document removal, not 'before remove' in the sense originally implied. A reader of the table alone (without reading the Architecture section) could reconstruct the wrong ordering. The parenthetical should be updated to reflect 'written after event cascade, before project document removal' or similar.

summary: All 8 round-1 findings have been addressed. 31/31 requirements remain covered. One new critical finding was introduced by the fix itself: the Architecture section's corrected cascade ordering (delete events → emit → delete projects) was NOT propagated to the ProjectHardDeleteJobTest description in the Testing Strategy, which still describes the old broken order (emit → delete events → delete projects). This creates a direct contradiction between Architecture and Testing Strategy — a developer following the test description would reintroduce the round-1 bug. One additional minor finding: the Audit event table parenthetical comment for project_hard_deleted still reads 'written before remove', which is now misleading given the corrected ordering. The spec fails on the one remaining critical finding.
